posts.title: Packages from Home
posts.description: Mail from home always cheered up the troops – but receiving a package was the ultimate gift for a soldier and his squad. Everybody shared in the bounty and held the ‘sender’ in the highest esteem. What was the best/worst thing you remember receiving in these special packages from home? I’ll start. As an infantry soldier living in the bush, the most treasured item Mom sent was Heinz 57 and Tabasco sauce to doctor up C-Rations. My worst was a 5-lb can of ham that was supposed to be refrigerated. posts.title: 2027 Traveling Wall Schedule
posts.description: We are delighted to share the 2027 national tour schedule for The Wall That Heals , our three-quarter-scale replica of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial and accompanying mobile Education Center. Beginning March 25 in Red Oak, North Carolina, The Wall That Heals will embark on a journey spanning more than 14,000 miles and 29 communities across the country before concluding its season in Nags Head, North Carolina, in November. Along the way, thousands of veterans, family members, students, and visitors will have the opportunity to experience the power of The Wall in their own communities. At every stop, we will honor the 58,281 men and women whose names are inscribed on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial and pay tribute to the more than three million Americans who served in the Vietnam War. Through remembrance, reflection, and education, The Wall That Heals helps ensure that their service and sacrifice continue to be understood and remembered by future generations. posts.title: Coast Guard Operations in Vietnam
posts.description: By Tom Edward How many of you knew the Coast Guard participated in the Vietnam War? Read the attached article to learn more about their role. On April 29, 1965 President Lyndon B. Johnson established a ‘Memorandum of the President’. That document initiated the process of the United States Coast Guard working in conjunction with the United States Navy to prevent communist troops from accessing South Vietnam. The day the Memorandum was signed, Coast Guard Squadron One (RONONE) was established. It consisted of 47 officers and 198 enlisted men. They had received their training in Coronado, California. Less than a week after the establishment of RONONE, six 82-foot U.S.C.G. cutters were in shipyards for the necessary modifications. Following the yardwork, they were transferred to the Philippines and subsequently rendezvoused with the escort ship USS Snohomish County (LST-1126).
